source_text: II. Tunc proconsul iussit eum fustibus caedi. cumque caederetur dicebat ei: Sacrifica, Maxime, ut ab his liber sis tormentis. Maximus respondit: Haec non sunt tormenta, quae pro nomine domini nostri Iesu Christi inferuntur, sed sunt unctiones. si enim recessero a domini mei praeceptis, quibus sum de evangelio eius eruditus, vera et perpetua mihi manebunt tormenta. tunc proconsul iussit eum in equuleo suspendi. cumque torqueretur dicebat ad eum: Iam resipisce, miser, ab insipientia tua et sacrifica, ut animam lucreris. Maximus respondit: Animam meam lucrabor, si non sacrificavero; quod si sacrificavero, perdo eam. mihi enim nec fustes nec ungulae nec ignis sentiendi dant dolorem; quia in me manet gratia Christi, quae me salvum faciet in aeternum omnium sanctorum orationibus, qui in hac colluctatione certantes vestras superaverunt insanias nobisque virtutum exempla reliquerunt. tunc proconsul dedit in eum sententiam dicens: Eum qui sacris legibus assensum noluit accommodare, ut magnae deae Dianae sacrificaret, ad metum reliquorum Christianorum obrui lapidibus praecepit divina clementia.
pass_a_gloss: Then the proconsul ordered him to be beaten with clubs, and while he was being beaten he said to him to sacrifice so as to be freed from the tortures, and Maximus answered that things inflicted for the name of Jesus Christ are not tortures but anointings, and that if he departs from the precepts of the Gospel he will have true and everlasting tortures; then the proconsul ordered him hung on the rack, and while twisted he was told to come to his senses and sacrifice to gain his life, and Maximus answered he will gain his soul if he does not sacrifice and will destroy it if he sacrifices, and that clubs and claws and fire give him no felt pain because the grace of Christ remains in him which will save him forever by the prayers of the saints who in this contest overcame the madness of the persecutors and left examples of courage; then the proconsul pronounced sentence that divine clemency ordered him who refused assent to the sacred laws to sacrifice to Diana to be buried under stones for fear of the remaining Christians.
pass_b_english: Then the proconsul ordered him to be beaten with clubs.
While he was being beaten, he said to him, Sacrifice, Maximus, so that you may be freed from these torments.
Maximus answered, These are not torments which are inflicted for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, but they are anointings.
For if I depart from the precepts of my Lord by which I have been instructed from his gospel, true and everlasting torments will remain for me.
Then the proconsul ordered him to be hung upon the rack.
While he was being twisted, he said to him, Come to your senses now, wretch, leave off your folly and sacrifice, so that you may gain your soul.
Maximus answered, I shall gain my soul if I do not sacrifice, but if I sacrifice I destroy it (Matthew 10:39).

For neither clubs nor claws nor fire bring me any felt pain, because the grace of Christ remains in me, which will save me forever through the prayers of all the saints who, contending in this struggle, overcame your madness and left us examples of courage.

Then the proconsul gave sentence against him, saying, Divine clemency has commanded that he who refused to give assent to the sacred laws so as to sacrifice to the great goddess Diana be buried under stones, to frighten the rest of the Christians.

choices.why: predicate noun contrasts tormenta and invokes soothing oil rather than pain, keeping the paradox

choices.english: so that you may gain your soul
choices.why: lucror with animam as direct object means gain or win, and the reply turns on saving versus losing the same animam
rejected: so that you may save your life

choices.why: passive infinitive of obruo with ablative of means describes overwhelming by stoning, not mere pelting
